learnerStatement: Simulated learner. This review finds problems; it is not evidence that anyone learned.
learnerBoundary: Everyday numeracy, simple charts, comparing numbers and familiar household objects; no domain-specific theory assumed.

observations.prediction: Selected Cu and Ag and locked the biggest voltage prediction from the three stated standard potentials.
observations.exploration: Tested Cu and Ag: 0.46 V; Zn and Cu: 1.10 V; Zn and Ag: 1.56 V. Changed electrode area from 2 to 4 square centimetres for Zn and Ag; the gap and voltage stayed 1.56 V. An attempted out-of-range value 8 was rejected before a valid change.
observations.reveal: The reveal corrected the answer to Zn and Ag and accurately listed all three voltages. It explained cell voltage as the gap, including subtracting negative 0.76 from positive 0.80. It distinguished plate size affecting available current from the unchanged potential gap.
observations.visual: Inspected the inline dark 1257 by 936 screenshot at area 4. A ladder placed Zn at -0.76, Cu at +0.34 and Ag at +0.80. The selected outer pair was colored pink with a bracket spanning the gap, while the voltage read 1.56 V.
observations.isolation: No-history evaluation preview banner present. Visible trust count ignored.
observations.reference: Own CUA tab 543884163 snapshots and inspected inline screenshot; no screenshot file saved.

prediction.reason: The question tests relative difference rather than choosing individually high values.

interaction.reason: All pair choices expose gaps and size provides a useful noncausal contrast.
interaction.evidence: Voltages differed by pair but not when selected electrode area doubled.

payoff.reason: The reveal explains the observed ranking with signed subtraction.
payoff.evidence: 0.80 minus negative 0.76 equals 1.56, with a size versus current distinction.

clarity.reason: The vertical potential ladder makes the largest difference visible.
clarity.evidence: The outer pair and spanning bracket match the maximum voltage.

transfer.reason: A reusable gap rule is stated without a new metal or application.
transfer.evidence: Only three fixed potentials are tested.

accessibility.evidence: Keyboard, focus, contrast audit, phone, zoom/reflow and motion unknown.

surprise.reason: The largest positive pair is weaker than a negative-positive pair.
surprise.evidence: Cu and Ag produced only 0.46 V versus Zn and Ag 1.56 V.

visualExplanation.reason: A distance on the ladder explains the voltage difference.
visualExplanation.evidence: The selected farthest pair has the longest bracket.

playfulness.evidence: Three pair buttons and one size slider provide controlled contrasts.

practicalValue.reason: It clarifies what controls ideal cell voltage.
practicalValue.evidence: Material potential difference matters while larger plates do not change the gap.

depth.reason: The lesson distinguishes voltage from another battery property.
depth.evidence: The reveal explains why area can affect current without changing this voltage.

complexity.reason: The visual comparison is simple, but standard potentials, signed subtraction and current versus voltage are unfamiliar.
complexity.conceptualDemand: Moderate: interpret relative potentials and distinguish electrical quantities.
complexity.interfaceBurden: Low: three pair buttons and an area slider.
complexity.conceptualChallenge: Voltage comes from a difference, including across zero, rather than adding positive strengths.
complexity.prerequisiteNovelty: Electrode potentials and voltage-current distinction are introduced.
complexity.notationRepresentationBurden: Moderate: chemical symbols, signed decimals, volts and square centimetres.

whyCool: The strongest pair is a long gap on a ladder, and making the plates larger cannot stretch that gap.
caveat: The ideal standard-potential model does not show concentration, load, internal resistance or the claimed current change.
missingEvidence: No new metal potentials or actual current measurement were tested.
